body:
## Summary

When a command inside `--isolated docker` dies of a **runtime self-abort on its own heap limit** — Node/V8's `FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory` — `start` reports it as an ordinary non-zero exit and explicitly states **`oomKilled=false`** in the kept-container footer. `--status` shows `status executed` / `exitCode 139` with no memory signal at all.

Every signal `start` currently consults is a *cgroup/container* signal, and a V8 self-abort is invisible to all of them: the process kills itself at its own `--max-old-space-size` cap long before the container's memory limit is reached, so `docker inspect` really does report `State.OOMKilled=false` and `memory.events` really does report `oom_kill 0`. Both readings are technically correct and together they produce a **false negative for "out of memory" every single time** a Node process hits its own heap cap.

The evidence is not missing — it is printed by the dying runtime into the very log `start` already reads a tail of (`readLogTail` / `readExitCodeFromLog`), a couple of KB above the `Exit Code:` footer.

## Reproduction

`start-command` 0.32.1 (latest), Docker 29.6.0, Linux.

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/upstream-repro && cd /tmp/upstream-repro
cat > oom.mjs <<'JS'
// Force a V8 heap-limit self-abort: gradual growth under a small old-space cap.
const held = [];
for (;;) held.push('x'.repeat(1024 * 1024));
JS
B64=$(base64 -w0 oom.mjs)
$ --isolated docker --image node:24 -- bash -c "echo $B64 | base64 -d > /tmp/oom.mjs; node --max-old-space-size=64 /tmp/oom.mjs"
```

<sub>The base64 detour is only needed because the direct form `$ --isolated docker --image node:24 -- node --max-old-space-size=64 -e "..."` loses its argument quoting before it reaches the container — filed separately as #164.</sub>

### Observed

Tail of `/tmp/start-command/logs/isolation/docker/<uuid>.log`:

```
<--- Last few GCs --->
[1:0xa485000]  790 ms: Mark-Compact 66.6 (99.8) -> 64.4 (194.2) MB, ... allocation failure; scavenge might not succeed

FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
----- Native stack trace -----
 1: 0x757658 node::OOMErrorHandler(char const*, v8::OOMDetails const&) [node]
 ...
Docker container "docker-1788423255481-l595xv" exited with code 139
Container kept because the command failed.

==================================================
Finished: 2026-09-03 08:14:20.707
Exit Code: 139
```

`$ --status 006e2eb8-5903-4c72-9934-45e1eed57fb5`:

```
  status executed
  exitCode 139
  options
    isolated docker
    isolationMode attached
```

`docker inspect --format '{{.State.OOMKilled}} {{.State.ExitCode}}'` → `false 139`.

So: exit **139**, no `oomKilled` field at all on the attached record, and nothing anywhere in `--status` says "this ran out of memory". A consumer that keys off `exitCode` + `oomKilled` concludes "arbitrary crash / forced kill", which is what happened downstream (below).

### Expected

`start` should carry a **memory-exhaustion observation** derived from the log tail, e.g.

```
  status executed
  exitCode 139
  memoryExhausted true
  memoryExhaustedReason "FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory"
```

and the kept-container footer should not assert the opposite of what is printed 8 lines above it:

```
Container kept for investigation: <name>
Reason: exitCode=139 oomKilled=false        <-- next to a FATAL ERROR heap-limit abort
```

## Real-world incident this comes from

Downstream: link-assistant/hive-mind#2189. A `solve` run under `--isolated docker` (image `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.15.1`, execution `0ea1c630-cfdf-477e-8528-29d175a7fe64`) died at 14:07:49Z. Preserved log tail:

```
[1:0x2c2be5c0] 106418040 ms: Mark-Compact 2121.9 (2169.0) -> 2121.9 (2160.8) MB, ... scavenge might not succeed
FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
...
11: 0x157aaad v8::internal::FixedArrayBuilder::EnsureCapacity(v8::internal::Isolate*, int) [node]
12: 0x15385ff v8::internal::Runtime_RegExpExecMultiple(int, unsigned long*, v8::internal::Isolate*) [node]

Container kept for investigation: dd1acfbe-3c01-4ffa-8c78-f825457f5813
Reason: exitCode=139 oomKilled=false
==================================================
Exit Code: 139
```

The `FATAL ERROR` line sits **2 102 bytes from EOF** — comfortably inside the existing 16 KiB `LOG_TAIL_BYTES` window. The downstream supervisor, reading `exitCode=139 oomKilled=false`, reported to the user:

```
cause=forced-kill — forced kill — memory (10.3 GB of 11.7 GB RAM available (12.2% used))
```

i.e. "killed for no reason on a machine with 10 GB free", for a process that had just told the log it ran out of memory. The wrong classification then selected the wrong recovery policy.

## Why the existing OOM handling does not cover this

#144/#148/#151 built out `State.OOMKilled` handling, and #151 correctly settled that the cgroup flag is an *observation*, never a verdict (`resolveOomObservation`, `status-formatter.js:109`). That work is sound — it is just structurally blind here:

| signal | V8 self-abort at its own cap |
|---|---|
| `docker inspect .State.OOMKilled` | `false` (kernel never OOM-killed anything) |
| `memory.events` `oom_kill` | `0` |
| container memory limit | never reached |
| exit code | `139` (SIGSEGV) or `134` (SIGABRT) — indistinguishable from a real crash |
| **runtime's own stderr** | **`FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit …`** |

Only the last row carries the information, and only `start` is positioned to read it before the container filesystem is cleaned up.

Note also that `oomKilled` is only ever attached in `enrichDetachedStatus`, so **attached** docker sessions (the repro above, and a large share of real use) have no memory field of any kind.

## Suggested fix (code)

Everything needed already exists in `src/lib/status-formatter.js`; `readLogTail(logPath, bytes = LOG_TAIL_BYTES)` is exactly the bounded primitive for this.

1. **Detect the marker from the tail** (new helper next to `readExitCodeFromLog`):

```js
// A runtime that aborts on its own heap limit is invisible to every cgroup
// signal: it dies below the container limit, so State.OOMKilled stays false.
// The only evidence is what the runtime printed on its way out.
const FATAL_MEMORY_PATTERNS = [
  /FATAL ERROR:[^\n]*Reached heap limit/,               // Node.js / V8
  /FATAL ERROR:[^\n]*Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit/,
  /JavaScript heap out of memory/,
  /Array buffer allocation failed/,
  /memory allocation of \d+ bytes failed/,              // Rust
  /fatal error: runtime: out of memory/,                // Go
  /std::bad_alloc/,                                     // C/C++
];

function readMemoryAbortFromLog(logPath) {
  if (!logPath) return null;
  const tail = readLogTail(logPath, 64 * 1024); // native stack traces are long
  if (tail === null) return null;
  for (const pattern of FATAL_MEMORY_PATTERNS) {
    const m = pattern.exec(tail);
    if (m) {
      const start = tail.lastIndexOf('\n', m.index) + 1;
      const end = tail.indexOf('\n', m.index);
      return { line: tail.slice(start, end < 0 ? undefined : end).trim() };
    }
  }
  return null;
}
```

A 64 KiB window rather than 16 KiB, because V8 prints a native stack trace *after* the marker; in the incident above the marker was 2 KB from EOF, but a longer trace could push it past 16 KiB.

2. **Expose it as an observation, never as a verdict** — same discipline #151 established for `oomKilled`. Only consult it when the run ended abnormally (`exitCode !== 0`), so a log that merely *quotes* the string cannot turn a clean run into a reported crash:

```js
if (enriched.exitCode !== 0 && enriched.exitCode !== null) {
  const memoryAbort = readMemoryAbortFromLog(record.logPath);
  if (memoryAbort) {
    enriched.memoryExhausted = true;
    enriched.memoryExhaustedReason = memoryAbort.line;
  }
}
```

plus the corresponding fields in `execution-store.js` (`toObject`, alongside `oomKilled`) and in the human formatter (`Memory Exhausted:  true`, next to `OOM Killed:`).

3. **Fix the kept-container footer.** `buildDockerKeptLogSnippet` (`docker-cleanup.js:146`) prints `Reason: exitCode=%s oomKilled=%s` from `docker inspect` alone. For exit `139`/`134` the flat `oomKilled=false` is actively misleading — either drop the field for those codes or add a line noting that a runtime self-abort is not visible to the container flag. This footer is the string downstream tooling greps.

4. **Apply it to attached sessions too**, not only `enrichDetachedStatus` — the log tail is available either way, and attached is where the repro (and much real use) lives.

## Workaround (what we do downstream today)

Hive Mind now re-derives the classification itself, since `start` cannot supply it: a bounded 64 KiB tail read of the same log, matched against the pattern table above, upgrading the kill cause to out-of-memory whenever the exit was abnormal — `src/child-exit.lib.mjs` (`FATAL_MEMORY_PATTERNS`, `findFatalMemoryMarker`) consumed by `src/session-kill-diagnostics.lib.mjs`. It works, but every `start` consumer has to reimplement it, and only after the fact — `start` is the component that still has the container and the log in hand.

## Related

- #144 (surface container resource exhaustion), #148, #151 (OOM flag is an observation, not a verdict)
- Downstream: link-assistant/hive-mind#2189
title: Docker isolation: a V8 heap-limit self-abort (exit 139/134) is reported with `oomKilled=false` and no memory signal in `--status`
